statement: The polynomial $2x^{3}-3x^{2}-11x+6$ has a root at $x=3$. (i) Factorise it completely. (ii) Find the quotient and remainder when it is divided by $x^{2}+x-2$. (iii) Hence solve $2x^{3}-3x^{2}-11x+6=0$.
solution: (i) Since $x=3$ is a root, $2x^{3}-3x^{2}-11x+6=(x-3)(2x^{2}+3x-2)=(x-3)(2x-1)(x+2)$. (ii) Dividing by $x^{2}+x-2$: $(x^{2}+x-2)(2x-5)=2x^{3}-3x^{2}-9x+10$; subtracting from the polynomial leaves $-2x-4$, so the quotient is $2x-5$ and the remainder is $-2x-4$. (iii) Roots are $x=3,\ \tfrac12,\ -2$.
